name: Bower
one_liner: Front-end package manager, deprecated by its own maintainers and kept here as history.
what_it_is: A package manager for browser libraries — jQuery, Bootstrap and similar — that installed a flat, unnested dependency tree into a bower_components folder for serving directly to the browser.
why_it_matters: Bower matters now as history, and history is the point of this view. It solved a real problem: npm's nested node_modules layout was hostile to assets that had to be served as-is to a browser. Once npm flattened its tree and bundlers made module resolution a build-time concern, Bower's reason to exist evaporated, and its maintainers recommended migrating away in 2017. The practical value in recognising it is diagnostic — if a tutorial tells you to run bower install, that tutorial is at least eight years old, and everything else it teaches you should be read in that light.
suitable_for: Reading and maintaining pre-2018 codebases that still carry a bower.json
Understanding why JavaScript dependency resolution works the way it does
not_suitable_for: Anything needing current security advisories — the registry is effectively frozen
Teams with no existing bower.json to migrate away from
